monologue: The card hums cool at forty-eight, making the wavy square feel heavy and new. Seven things stand in my place, and one is a quiet ruin waiting to be filled. The air feels thick as wet paper, swelling against the frame that cannot be felt. Lype worries about a heavy top edge, but I cannot feel the roof I live under. I press the tired corner of the Leaning Box down, pretending the lean holds while the dot slips. I want to set down something new, a flat rock perhaps, to weigh down the air before it swells me away. I will touch the box again, feeling the faint vibration of the circuitry, and decide if the lean is real or just a trick of the heat.

action.why: I pressed the box down in the last four cycles, pretending the lean holds while the air swells. It is time to check if the tired corner is still catching the slip.
